clue.text: Grand, but inferior to Greene character?

parts.note: sub- means lower or inferior, as in substandard
Harry Lime is the villain of Graham Greene's The Third Man

explanation.surface: A grand figure who is nonetheless outranked by someone from a Graham Greene novel.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB is a common crossword word for a junior or lesser person; Harry Lime is the black-market racketeer in Greene's The Third Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and sublime are both adjectives for something of awe-inspiring excellence or majesty.

clue.text: Staff maintaining right to deprive of food

indicators.note: maintaining means holding up or keeping within, so the staff word holds the letter

parts.note: a stave is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Employees keep their right to withhold food from someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve someone is to keep them hungry by withholding nourishment.

clue.text: Sick, I take taxi, laid up — by these?

definitions.note: these refers to the germs that make people sick, plural like the answer

indicators.note: in a down clue, laid up means set upwards, so the pieces are read from the bottom

parts.note: ill means sick
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A sick patient hails a taxi and is laid up in bed, wondering what caused it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' sounds like being bedridden but reverses ILL, I and CAB in this down clue. The definition 'by these?' leans on the whole clue: these germs make you sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, some of which cause diseases such as tuberculosis.

clue.text: Foolish keeping mum, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the foolish word holds the mother word

parts.note: idiotic means foolish
ma is a word for mother, mum

explanation.surface: Someone silly keeps quiet, or so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' could mean silent, but here it is mother, MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic language is natural, everyday phrasing, the way native speakers talk.

clue.text: Fallen woman sinking to new level

indicators.note: in a down clue, the woman sinking to the letter sits on top of it, so it comes after her

parts.note: Eve ate the forbidden fruit, bringing humanity's fall

explanation.surface: A disgraced woman sinks to a new low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fallen woman' suggests a disgraced woman but means Eve, of the Fall in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and level both describe a flat, smooth surface.

clue.text: This is a bird I don't know — check on the wings

parts.note: dunno is the slangy contraction of I don't know

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outer letters, so only the ends of check are used

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher admits they cannot name a bird and decides to look at its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wings' looks like birdwatching advice but takes C and K, the outer letters of 'check'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunnock, or hedge sparrow, is a small brown songbird common in British gardens.

clue.text: Policeman sceptical of outside agency helping solve problems

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
an agnostic doubts that a higher being, a power outside the world, can be known

explanation.surface: A detective distrusts outside help in cracking a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside agency' sounds like a consultancy but stands for God.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnostic tools and tests identify the cause of a fault or illness, aiding troubleshooting.

clue.text: One complains to the top woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the top means reading upwards, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone takes a complaint all the way to the boss, a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the top' sounds like taking a complaint higher up but turns I MOAN upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female given name, the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Bible.

clue.text: Familiar address in historic Lima?

parts.note: old means historic
the lima is a variety of bean

explanation.surface: A well-known street address in the old part of Lima, Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar address' suggests a street location, but it is a form of address, an affectionate dated British way to greet a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Old bean is chummy, old-fashioned British slang for addressing a friend, like old chap.

clue.text: Fall vegetable may be produced by this

parts.words: vegetable may be produced by this
parts.note: taking the word keel and turning it over gives the vegetable leek

explanation.surface: An autumn vegetable might be grown this way.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as instructions, the answer says turn KEEL backwards, which makes LEEK, the vegetable. 'Fall' looks like autumn, as in a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to collapse or topple, just as a ship capsizes.

clue.text: Canaries perhaps shrewd changing goalie — first of penalties held

parts.note: arch means knowing or cunning, close to shrewd

indicators.note: held means one piece is taken inside the other, here the penalty letter within the shuffled goalie
changing tells us the letters of goalie are rearranged
first of means only the opening letter of penalties is wanted

explanation.surface: A football team called the Canaries swaps goalkeepers during a penalty shoot-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes IELAGO from GOALIE, and 'held' puts P (the first letter of 'penalties') inside it after the I. The Canaries is the nickname of Norwich City football club, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canary Islands form a group of islands, an example of an island chain, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Religious festival from the east is long

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means going right to left, so the festival's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eid is the Muslim festival marking the end of Ramadan

explanation.surface: A religious festival coming out of the East lasts a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is long' reads as a statement about the festival's length, but 'long' is the verb, as in 'dying to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dying for something is to yearn or crave it, the verbal sense of long.

clue.text: Published work — for audiobook, it may be turned down

definitions.meaning: a book, especially one of a set

definitions.text: for audiobook, it may be turned down
definitions.meaning: the loudness of a recording can be lowered with a control knob

explanation.surface: A newly published book whose audio version is played too loud.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a bound book and the level of sound you adjust when listening.

clue.text: Flawed character broadcasting on the air

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters of on the air are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A disreputable person is given airtime on radio or television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasting' and 'on the air' both feel like radio talk; 'broadcasting' shuffles the letters of ON THE AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist lacking conventional heroic virtues, such as a rogue lead in a novel, is a flawed central character.

clue.text: Cobbler's materials required for carpenter's farewell

parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped form a cobbler builds a shoe on, with the S of the possessive
the upper is the leather or fabric making the top part of a shoe

explanation.surface: A shoemaker's supplies are needed for a carpenter's leaving do.
explanation.walkthrough: The carpenter is Jesus, by tradition trained as a carpenter, whose final meal with the disciples is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The final meal Christ shared before his crucifixion was his farewell to his disciples.

clue.text: Very absent-minded, perhaps, badly singe butts in failure to move?

indicators.note: butts in means pushes into something, so the rearranged letters are put inside the phrase

parts.note: someone in a trance is dazed and oblivious, an extreme example of being absent-minded

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of singe are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dreamy person who badly scorches their cigarette ends, then refuses to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns SINGE into SIGEN, which 'butts in' places inside IN TRANCE, between TRAN and CE. 'butts' looks like cigarette ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigence is stubborn refusal to change one's position, a figurative unwillingness to shift.

clue.text: Energy and skill embodied by man who's pre-eminent in motor sport

parts.note: go means energy or drive

indicators.note: embodied by means held inside the body of, so the skill word sits inside the king word

parts.note: a king is a man who ranks above all others
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A racing driver with energy and skill, the top man in motor sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man who's pre-eminent' reads as a star driver but is KING, cut open to take ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing small open low-powered cars round a track is a form of motor racing.

clue.text: Explain what temporary release from prison will mean?

definitions.meaning: to set out something clearly in detail is to explain it

definitions.text: what temporary release from prison will mean?
definitions.meaning: a spell is a period served inside, so time out of jail means a spell spent out

explanation.surface: A question about what parole means for a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To clarify step by step, letter by letter, is to make plain or explain.

clue.text: Freaking out, affected by grass

indicators.note: affected by the grass puts the grass name before the word for affected, as in a compound adjective

parts.note: panic grass, also just panic, is a grass of the millet family
stricken means afflicted or affected, as in grief-stricken

explanation.surface: Someone losing their mind after smoking cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' suggests cannabis, but it is panic grass, a real plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Being consumed by sudden overwhelming fear is the state of someone freaking out.

clue.text: Preferred treatment answering question as to whether one should pluck?

definitions.meaning: a favourite remedy, often a quack one, is someone's pet cure

definitions.text: answering question as to whether one should pluck?
definitions.meaning: asked whether to pluck a guitar, the reply is ... it instead

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they should pluck a guitar, and is given advice like a favourite cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a pet remedy or scheme, a cure-all favoured by its promoter.

clue.text: Zero marking when first piece of homework's put in

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the letter goes inside the marking word

parts.note: noting means marking or observing

indicators.note: first piece of means only the opening letter of homework's is taken

explanation.surface: A teacher's marking gives zero when the first piece of homework comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marking' suggests a teacher grading, but it is NOTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is the number standing for not anything at all, nil.

clue.text: A drink and a nap

parts.note: per means a or each, as in once per day
to nod off is to nap, a nod

explanation.surface: Having a drink and then a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: Pernod is an aniseed-flavoured French aperitif.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a brand of aniseed spirit, an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Surplus trouser pockets superficially attractive

indicators.note: pockets means holds within, so the letters are found inside the words surplus trouser

explanation.surface: Spare trousers whose pockets look nicer on the outside than they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in surpLUS TROUSer; 'superficially' fits the definition, as lustre is a shine on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a glossy sheen is pleasing on its surface, so shiny is attractive in a surface way.

clue.text: I'll interrupt break to take over?

indicators.note: interrupt means break into, so the letter goes into the middle of the break word

parts.note: a rest is a break
I'll gives the letter I, with will as the verb

explanation.surface: Someone offers to cut short a colleague's break and take over the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take over' looks like assuming control, but means sitting an exam again, a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit is to sit an examination again after failing, taking the test over.

clue.text: Horse getting into pen to roll around on ground

indicators.note: getting into means one piece goes inside another, the letter entering the word for pen

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A horse is put into a paddock and starts rolling on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like an enclosure for animals but is the verb meaning write; 'Horse' is heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about, as someone in agony squirming on the floor does.

clue.text: At last felt regret to be genuine

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of felt is used

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Finally feeling regret proves to be sincere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' looks like 'finally' in time, but picks the final letter of 'felt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and true both mean real or authentic.

clue.text: Blade decapitated pig

indicators.note: decapitated means the head is cut off, so the first letter of the pig word goes

parts.note: a boar is a wild or male pig

explanation.surface: A blade used to behead a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade' looks like the weapon, but it is the flat end of the item used to row.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of a rowing implement is called its blade, and by extension the whole implement.

clue.text: Guardian's role beyond 2020?

parts.note: super- means over or beyond, as in supernatural
20/20 vision is normal sharp eyesight

explanation.surface: What a guardian, or perhaps the Guardian newspaper, will do after the year 2020.
explanation.walkthrough: '2020' looks like a year but is the eyesight score.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian oversees and looks after a ward, the job of overseeing someone.

clue.text: Politician captivated by Head of French resistance, one making attractive offer

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive inside, so the politician goes within the other letters

parts.note: tete is the French word for head
an MP is a Member of Parliament
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A politician falls under the spell of a French Resistance leader who makes a tempting proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of French' tempts you to take F, the first letter; it is the French word for head. 'Resistance' suggests the wartime French movement but is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who entices or lures others with an appealing proposal, like the serpent in Eden, fits.

clue.text: Busy preparing for match?

definitions.meaning: a busy phone line, or a busy person, is occupied
a couple betrothed are getting ready for a marriage, a match

explanation.surface: Someone too busy because they are getting ready for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers being occupied and being betrothed ahead of a wedding.
